lessons.name: Berry connection, gauge transformation and closed-loop geometric phase
locators: Chapter 6 section 5, printed p. 14, Eqs. (5.15)–(5.22): Berry gauge transformation and curvature
Chapter 6 section 5, printed p. 15, Eqs. (5.23)–(5.27): gauge-invariant curvature and spin-1/2 solid angle
lessons.workedExample: For |n+>=(cos(theta/2), exp(i phi) sin(theta/2)), A_phi=-sin²(theta/2). At theta=pi/3 the latitude loop encloses Omega=pi and gamma=-pi/2 modulo 2pi.
lessons.assumptions: An isolated, normalized, smooth nondegenerate instantaneous eigenstate followed adiabatically around a closed parameter-space loop; distinguish dynamic from geometric phase.
nonClaims: The connection changes under local phase-gauge choices; physical closed-loop holonomy is gauge invariant modulo 2pi under allowed single-valued gauge changes.
An adiabatic approximation fails near uncontrolled degeneracies or rapid driving; this example does not establish any experimental quantum-hardware performance.

lessons.name: First Born scattering amplitude, momentum transfer and validity
locators: Chapter 7 section 7.3.1, printed p. 148, Eqs. (7.3.30)–(7.3.33): weak-potential amplitude and wave-number transfer
Chapter 7 section 7.3.1, printed p. 149, Eq. (7.3.37): Yukawa potential example
lessons.workedExample: For V(r)=beta exp(-mu r)/r, f_Born(K)=-2m beta/[hbar²(K²+mu²)]. At m=hbar=beta=mu=k=1 and theta=pi/2, K=sqrt(2), f=-2/3 and d sigma/d Omega=4/9.
lessons.assumptions: Elastic nonrelativistic spinless potential scattering, short-range Yukawa force, reduced mass m and wave-number transfer K=k_out-k_in with |K|=2k sin(theta/2); Born series first order requires a sufficiently weak scattering perturbation.
nonClaims: K in the exponential has inverse-length units and is not a physical momentum unless multiplied by hbar.
A high incident energy may help a short-range weak-potential approximation, but does not universally guarantee Born convergence or establish QFT scattering amplitudes.

lessons.name: Two spin-1/2 states: triplet and singlet decomposition
locators: Chapter 10 section 2, printed p. 4, Eqs. (2.8)–(2.10): 1/2 tensor 1/2 decomposes as 1 direct-sum 0
Chapter 10 section 2, printed p. 5, Eqs. (2.17)–(2.18): normalized symmetric triplet m=0 and antisymmetric singlet
lessons.workedExample: Triplet states are |up up>, (|up down>+|down up>)/sqrt(2), |down down>; singlet is (|up down>-|down up>)/sqrt(2). Total S² eigenvalues are 2 hbar² and 0 respectively.
lessons.assumptions: Two distinguishable spin-1/2 factors with total S=S1+S2, standard Condon–Shortley relative-phase convention and hbar-normalized ladder operators.
nonClaims: The spin factor is not a complete state for identical particles without satisfying total exchange symmetry including spatial degrees of freedom.
Clebsch–Gordan coefficients are basis-change data; their existence is not an experiment proving particle entanglement or a historical relationship between catalog entities.
